name: Mithredath
title: The Persian Treasurer
summary: Mithredath (also known as Mithredath) was the treasurer under the Persian king Cyrus the Great. He was tasked with counting and delivering the sacred vessels from the temple in Jerusalem that Nebuchadnezzar had taken to Babylon, so they could be returned to the Jewish people. He plays a small but important role in the restoration of temple service in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Delivery of the Temple Vessels
keyEvents.description: Mithredath, who was treasurer under King Cyrus, was tasked with counting and handing over the sacred vessels from the temple in Jerusalem to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.

keyEvents.title: The Counting of the Temple Articles
keyEvents.description: Mithredath delivered gold and silver bowls, knives, cups, and basins—5400 items made of gold and silver in total—to be brought back to Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Cyrus's Decree on Rebuilding
keyEvents.description: Cyrus issued a decree that the temple in Jerusalem should be rebuilt and ordered that the sacred vessels be returned—which enabled Mithredath's role.

keyEvents.title: Letter of Complaint to Artaxerxes
keyEvents.description: Another person named Mitredat (possibly a different individual) was among those who wrote a letter of complaint to King Artaxerxes to stop the rebuilding of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: The Temple Vessels Arrive in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: The holy temple vessels that Mitredat had handed over were brought back to Jerusalem by Sheshbazzar along with the returning exiles.
